messages.author: 3ea57457192f4f3b
messages.subject: R and MySQL
parts:
I am stuck with an old problem. I would like to develop a web
application that stores R dataframes in a MySQL database. I use the
CRAN package RMySQL. However, the mappings between R and MySQL
datatypes are ambiguous, especially for factors.

Both R-factors and R-character vectors are mapped to MySQL strings.
This is inconvenient, however, not the biggest problem. My biggest
issue is ordered factors: When ordered factor that is stored to MySQL,
it too is converted to a string, and loses it's ordering.

Any suggestions on this? Maybe it would be possible to map ordered
factors to MySQL 'ENUM' datatype (http://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/5.0/
en/enum.html)? Enum seem to be very similar to ordered factors in the
sense that they have an index, and associated labels.

messages.author: 10129ceeb6e8c4cb
messages.subject: Re: R and MySQL
parts:
I haven't used rapache yet, but i've had the same problem with RMySQL
more generally.

Try using factor(foo, levels = c(...,....))

It's annoying but it works, you'll just have to hardcode the factor
order you'd like.

I hope that helps, I could be way off base thoug.

x <- gl(2, 4, 8)
> levels(x) <- c("foo", "bar")
> x
[1] foo foo foo foo bar bar bar bar
Levels: foo bar
> ordered(x)
[1] foo foo foo foo bar bar bar bar
Levels: foo < bar
> x <- factor(x, levels = c("foo", "bar"))
> x
[1] foo foo foo foo bar bar bar bar
Levels: foo bar
> ordered(x)
[1] foo foo foo foo bar bar bar bar
Levels: foo < bar
> x <- factor(x, levels = c("bar", "foo"))
> x
[1] foo foo foo foo bar bar bar bar
Levels: bar foo
> ordered(x)
[1] foo foo foo foo bar bar bar bar
Levels: bar < foo
